claim_verdicts.evidence: 12.1: 'A lexeme is a string ... normalized so that different forms of the same word are made alike. For example, normalization almost always includes folding upper-case letters to lower-case'; 12.6.2: 'The simple dictionary template operates by converting the input token to lower case ... the lower-cased form of the word is returned as the normalized lexeme.' 12.3.3: 'Ranking attempts to measure how relevant documents are to a particular query, so that when there are many matches the most relevant ones can be shown first.'

11.2: 'GIN indexes are "inverted indexes" ... An inverted index contains a separate entry for each component value, and can efficiently handle queries that test for the presence of specific component values.' 12.1: 'Full text searches can be accelerated using indexes (Section 12.9).'

11.2 B-tree: 'The optimizer can also use a B-tree index for queries involving the pattern matching operators LIKE and ~ if the pattern is a constant and is anchored to the beginning of the string — for example, col LIKE 'foo%' or col ~ '^foo', but not col LIKE '%bar'.' EXPLAIN output not run (Bash unavailable in this session); the doc sentence settles the index part.

9.7.1: 'If pattern does not contain percent signs or underscores, then the pattern only represents the string itself; in that case LIKE acts like the equals operator.' 9.7: 'The pattern matching operators of all three kinds do not support nondeterministic collations.' So no accent-insensitive comparison is available to LIKE in 17; 'a' and 'à' are different characters.
